arxiv-2105-13509.title: Learning to Stylize Novel Views
arxiv-2105-13509.creator: Hsin-Ping Huang, Hung-Yu Tseng, Saurabh Saini, Maneesh Singh, Ming-Hsuan Yang
arxiv-2105-13509.description: Abstract We tackle a 3D scene stylization problem — generating stylized images of a scene from arbitrary novel views given a set of images of the same scene and a reference image of the desired style as inputs. Direct solution of combining novel view synthesis and stylization approaches lead to results that are blurry or not consistent across different views.

arxiv-2106-11885.title: Efficient uncertainty quantification for Monte Carlo dose calculations using importance (re-)weighting
arxiv-2106-11885.creator: P. Stammer, L. Burigo, O. Jäkel, M. Frank, N. Wahl
arxiv-2106-11885.description: Abstract The high precision and conformity of intensity-modulated particle therapy (IMPT) comes at the cost of susceptibility to treatment uncertainties in particle range and patient set-up. Dose uncertainty quantification and mitigation, which is usually based on sampled error scenarios, however becomes challenging when computing the dose with computationally expensive but accurate Monte Carlo (MC) simulations.

arxiv-2305-14775.title: Measuring the Knowledge Acquisition-Utilization Gap in Pretrained Language Models
arxiv-2305-14775.creator: Amirhossein Kazemnejad, Mehdi Rezagholizadeh, Prasanna Parthasarathi, Sarath Chandar
arxiv-2305-14775.description: Abstract While pre-trained language models (PLMs) have shown evidence of acquiring vast amounts of knowledge, it remains unclear how much of this parametric knowledge is actually usable in performing downstream tasks. We propose a systematic framework to measure parametric knowledge utilization in PLMs.

arxiv-2306-04445.title: Multi-modal Latent Diffusion
arxiv-2306-04445.creator: Mustapha Bounoua, Giulio Franzese, Pietro Michiardi
arxiv-2306-04445.description: Abstract Multi-modal data-sets are ubiquitous in modern applications, and multi-modal Variational Autoencoders are a popular family of models that aim to learn a joint representation of the different modalities. However, existing approaches suffer from a coherence–quality tradeoff, where models with good generation quality lack generative coherence across modalities, and vice versa.

arxiv-2309-16067.title: The Polarized Cosmic Hand: IXPE Observations of PSR B1509-58/MSH 15 − - 5 2 Facilities: ATCA, CXO , IXPE
arxiv-2309-16067.creator: Roger W. Romani, Josephine Wong, Niccoló Di Lalla, Nicola Omodei, Fei Xie, C.-Y. Ng, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Alessandro Di Marco, Niccoló Bucciantini, Maura Pilia, Patrick Slane, Martin C. Weisskopf, Simon Johnston, Marta Burgay, Deng Wei, Yi-Jung Yang, Shumeng Zhang, Lucio A. Antonelli, Matteo Bachett
arxiv-2309-16067.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roger W. Romani, Josephine Wong, Niccoló Di Lalla, Nicola Omodei, Fei Xie, C.-Y. Ng, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Alessandro Di Marco, Niccoló Bucciantini, Maura Pilia, Patrick Slane, Martin C. Weisskopf, Simon Johnston, Marta Burgay, Deng Wei, Yi-Jung Yang, Shumeng Zhang, Lucio A. Antonelli, Matteo Bachett. We describe IXPE polarization observations of the Pulsar Wind Nebula (PWN) MSH 15 − - 5 2 , the ‘Cosmic Hand’. We find X-ray polarization across the PWN, with B field vectors generally aligned with filamentary X-ray structures.

arxiv-2403-07730.title: Mechanisms of Elevated Temperature Galling in Hardfacings
arxiv-2403-07730.creator: Samuel R. Rogers, David Stewart, Paul Taplin, David Dye
arxiv-2403-07730.description: Abstract The galling mechanism of Tristelle 5183, an Fe-based hardfacing alloy, was investigated at elevated temperature. The test was performed using a bespoke galling rig. Adhesive transfer and galling were found to occur, as a result of shear at the adhesion boundary and the activation of an internal shear plane within one of the tribosurfaces.

arxiv-2407-04436.title: A Tunneling Method for Nonlinear Multi-objective Optimization Problems
arxiv-2407-04436.creator: Bikram Adhikary, Md Abu Talhamainuddin Ansary
arxiv-2407-04436.description: Abstract In this paper, a tunneling method is developed for nonlinear multi-objective optimization problems. The proposed method is free from any kind of priori chosen parameter or ordering information of objective functions. Using this method, global Pareto front can be generated for non-convex problems with more than one local front.

arxiv-2509-21580.title: Characterizations of Strongly Quasiconvex Functions
arxiv-2509-21580.creator: Nicolas Hadjisavvas, Felipe Lara
arxiv-2509-21580.description: Abstract We provide new necessary and sufficient conditons for ensuring strong quasiconvexity in the nonsmooth case and, as a consequence, we provide a proof for the differentiable case. Furthermore, we improve the quadratic growth property for strongly quasiconvex functions. Keywords : Generalized convexity; Strong quasiconvexity Mathematics Subject Classification: 90C26; 90C30.

pmc-10597090.creator: S Zhou, S Abelson, K Stojanovski
pmc-10597090.description: BackgroundAsian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) sexual and gender minority (SGM) young and emerging adults are an especially high-risk group to consider in mental health research, holding multiple marginalized identities & report discrimination based on race/ethnicity & immigration status at double the rate of overall SGM youth.

pmc-11416024.title: Exploring innovative strides in radiolabeled nanoparticle progress for multimodality cancer imaging and theranostic applications
pmc-11416024.creator: Atena Najdian, Davood Beiki, Milad Abbasi, Ali Gholamrezanezhad, Hojjat Ahmadzadehfar, Ali Mohammad Amani, Mehdi Shafiee Ardestani, Majid Assadi
pmc-11416024.description: Multimodal imaging unfolds as an innovative approach that synergistically employs a spectrum of imaging techniques either simultaneously or sequentially. The integration of computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), positron emission tomography (PET), and optical imaging (OI) results in a comprehensive and complementary understanding of complex biological processes.

pmc-11429318.title: Factors Affecting Cell Viability during the Enzymatic Dissociation of Human Endocrine Tumor Tissues
pmc-11429318.creator: Anastasia Shcherbakova, Marina Utkina, Anna Valyaeva, Nano Pachuashvili, Ekaterina Bondarenko, Liliya Urusova, Sergey Popov, Natalya Mokrysheva, Erxi Wu
pmc-11429318.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryOur study identified specific conditions for optimal cell viability in enzymatic dissociation protocols across various endocrine tumors. For adrenal medullary tumors, the critical factor was the dissociation time, with 20 min of incubation proving most effective. In the case of adrenocortical tumors, using Collagenase IV or the MTDK enzyme kit, along with a post-dissociation procedure involving a debris removal kit, resulted in higher cell viability.

pmc-11525641.title: Dynamic photomask directed lithography based on electrically stimulated nematic liquid crystal architectures
pmc-11525641.creator: Mengjun Liu, Ruizhi Yang, Zhenghao Guo, Kexu Chen, Haoqiang Feng, Han Lu, Shijian Huang, Minmin Zhang, Huapeng Ye, Lingling Shui
pmc-11525641.description: Lithography technology is a powerful tool for preparing complex microstructures through projecting patterns from static templates with permanent features onto samples. To simplify fabrication and alignment processes, dynamic photomask for multiple configurations preparation becomes increasingly noteworthy. Hereby, we report a dynamic photomask by assembling the electrically stimulated nematic liquid crystal (NLC) into multifarious architectures.

pmc-11590586.title: A systematic review on reverse-zoonosis: Global impact and changes in transmission patterns
pmc-11590586.creator: Zakaria Al Noman, Shadia Tasnim, Rony Ibne Masud, Tasnia Tabassum Anika, Md. Saiful Islam, Al Muksit Mohammad Taufiquer Rahman, Md. Tanvir Rahman
pmc-11590586.description: Reverse zoonosis or zooanthroponosis is the transfer of pathogens from humans to animals. Although less studied than zoonotic diseases, this phenomenon poses significant risks to both animal and public health. The increasing human-animal interactions driven by urbanization, globalization, and environmental changes have exacerbated the occurrence of reverse zoonosis.

pmc-12578998.title: Evaluation of non-indigenous biological assessment tools using benthic macroinvertebrates in a regulated river in the semi-arid region of Iran
pmc-12578998.creator: Fakhrieh Mohseni, Mohammad Nemati Varnosfaderany, Alireza Soffianian, Sima Fakheran
pmc-12578998.description: Benthic macroinvertebrates are widely used as key indicators in the biomonitoring of aquatic ecosystems, particularly in fragile ecosystems downstream of dams. Nevertheless, the use of non-indigenous biological tools requires regional evaluation, especially for developing countries and rivers with regulated flow in semi-arid regions. The Zayandehrud River is a perennial river in central Iran.

pmc-13582745.title: IMPACT: A Generative AI Prompt Framework for Scaling Instructional Video Design
pmc-13582745.creator: Mohit Gupta, Jake Aumeier, Smrithi Upadhyayula, Aidan Dulaney, Alexander Wu, James Willig, Natalie Bavli
pmc-13582745.description: Generative AI can transform lectures into asynchronous learning materials, but pedagogical quality depends on rigorous prompt engineering. We developed IMPACT, a six-component prompt-engineering framework, and applied it to design a six-stage video pipeline. Trainee-faculty co-creation produced 22 pre-clerkship hematology videos and was associated with positive trainee contributor perceptions.Supplementary InformationThe online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40670-026-02784-7.
